findings.title: Edit video (and API) cloud runs of fuobe-evolution are priced as 5 s whatever the clip, and no clip window is checked
findings.where: src/lib/catalog/models.ts (fuobe-evolution: defaults { duration: 5, ... }); src/lib/catalog/plan.ts estimateCost / clipEditSeconds; src/server/generations.ts ~1570; src/lib/catalog/clip-windows.ts
findings.detail: Under LTX-2.3, duration set num_frames, so the default 5 s was what was made and billed. fal's VACE depth route has match_input_num_frames on and no duration or num_frames mapping, so the clip's own length is rendered. But planGeneration merges model.defaults, so params.duration = 5 always, and estimateCost uses params.duration before clipEditSeconds/sourceDuration. The server's re-price for a clip edit (generations.ts) also passes plan.params with duration 5. The composer's cloud half has no length control, and Edit video lists fuobe-evolution on the cloud (modelsFor v2v). This is a regression: a direct cloud Evolution run shows a fixed $0.50 at 720p. fal bills frames ÷ 16: a 20 s clip at 30 fps is about $3.75. fuobe-shorts on the same route has no default duration, so it is priced by the clip's length. Neither model has a SOURCE_SECONDS window, so a clip over 241 frames is sent whole to fal's VACE, which allows at most 241 frames. Before, LTX made 5 s from any clip.
findings.evidence: A scratch vitest probe (outside the repo) ran planGeneration on {modelId fuobe-evolution, engine cloud, op v2v, video only} and got params.duration 5. estimateCost with sourceDuration 20 gave 0.5, and with 4, 10 or 30 s it was also 0.5. The same probe on fuobe-shorts gave 0.4 / 1 / 3 (2 at 20 s).
findings.fix: Move duration: 5 into engineDefaults.open, since only the GPU half has durations [3,4,5]. Give the cloud half a window, and price direct runs by frames ÷ 16 (Shorts' originalBilledSeconds / billFps), or keep fuobe-evolution's cloud route out of Edit video. Add a test that a direct cloud run's price follows the clip.

findings.title: The cloud sends the direction frame as first_frame_url, while the GPU graph uses it as VACE reference_image; the endpoint has ref_image_urls

findings.detail: In video-evolution-wan22-fun-vace, node 15 WanVaceToVideo takes the direction frame as reference_image and starts from the noised clip latent. The cloud sends the same frame as first_frame_url, which pins frame 0, and drops VACE references. fal's live depth schema (31 inputs, fetched in this review) does have ref_image_urls. This copies Fuobe Shorts' cloud recipe, not the GPU Evolution graph, which the brief asked to mirror 'as far as the hosted endpoint allows'. The docs say the cloud runs 'the way Fuobe Shorts runs it' but never note that the frame's role differs. The test pins the current choice in place.

fix.finalSummary:
Cloud engine: Fuobe Evolution runs fal's hosted Wan 2.2 Fun VACE depth, the GPU's model. Per piece of up to 10 s, a direction frame from hosted Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 (first 3 references) is now sent as VACE's reference (ref_image_urls), as the GPU graph does; the clip's sound goes back on; the run is priced first. Because the endpoint has no strength field, the change level shapes only the direction frame, and the page, the estimate and Settings say so. Direct cloud runs from Edit video or the API are now priced on the clip's frames ÷ 16 and held to 17–241 frames; this also applies to Fuobe Shorts and Genjutsu Restyle on the same endpoint. Fuobe Marketing Image's Standalone shot is GPU-only, and the cloud says so in its menu. Fuobe Speak's labels, the dop-mixed-media eval rule and the GPU's 24-key paths are unchanged from the implement stage.
Open engine (ComfyUI): unchanged. Evolution keeps the denoise Change control, 3/4/5 s, a required direction frame, 480p/720p, and its 5 s default. The Standalone shot keeps BiRefNet + 2509 + White_to_Scene.
Verified vs built: all of this is checked by unit and API tests plus demo-mode browser checks. Nothing was rendered: no GPU, no ComfyUI and no paid key were used. Unverified: fal's preprocess on an RGB clip, how well the VACE reference plus depth carries each change level, fal's behaviour for clips above 30 fps sent whole, and the first dop-mixed-media run, which needs paid keys.
Public sign-up: no new route or file path. request-schema accepts params.sourceFps, a price hint the server's own header read overrides. Guests and accounts get what they had: accounts run on their own ComfyUI (open engine, free), where none of the cloud pricing applies; Marketing Studio stays self-hosted only for visitors.
left: A hosted Standalone shot needs a step that puts the cut-out on white. Nothing hosted does it; it could be built as an in-server composite before 2509 + the White_to_Scene LoRA by URL (and Lightning) on fal-ai/qwen-image-edit-plus-lora.
Not yet measured: whether the direction frame works better as the VACE reference or as first_frame_url. The evolution eval suite can compare the two once paid keys exist.
Clips above 30 fps sent whole to fal's VACE (no temporal_downsample_factor on a direct run): fal's behaviour is unknown. Today they are counted at full rate for the 241-frame window and the price.

The browser checks still expect old model names: popcorn-evolution's Storyboard 'next-scene LoRA' check and marketing-originals' open-engine Photodump and Fashion checks (Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 on the GPU, from before 244bed92).
secret-box's replaced-key test can fail under the full run's load.

Follow-ups carried from the implement stage: Shorts' GPU first-frame edit is capped at 2 references; Marketing Image runs Qwen-Image 2.1 on the GPU vs 2511 in the cloud; the audio loop's cloud length is held to the GPU's 600 s limit.
The docs pass may want a FEATURES line for engineNote and for the cloud Standalone note.
